stories.body: LUDINGTON, MI – The Lake Michigan caferry Badger’s 2026 sailing season ended on Sunday, Oct. 11 when she docked for the winter at her Ludington, MI, home port. The Badger, operated by Lake Michigan Carferry, a part of Interlake Maritime Services, offers the largest cross-lake passenger service on the Great Lakes and an authentic steamship experience. The four-hour, 60-mile cruise takes passengers, autos, RVs, tour buses, motorcycles, bicycles, and commercial trucks across Lake Michigan between Ludington and Manitowoc, WI. Badger leaving Manitowoc on September 28. [Roger LeLievre]

shippingNews.postTitle: USCG Spar Towed to Fraser Shipyards

stories.body: Tug Nels J of Heritage/Dean Marine came down from its normal Two Harbors assignment Thursday to assist fleetmate and Superior-based tug Helen H in towing USCGC Spar from its base on Minnesota Point to Fraser Shipyards, where it will receive additional work after being idled this summer. Note: permission to fly within 3000 feet of SPAR was obtained in writing prior to drone flight. Spar under tow. [David Schauer] David Schauer

todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: Lake Superior is currently under a 29.9 inch trough associated with a 29.5 inch Colorado Low. To the north, a 30.4 inch high is sprawled out over central Canada. By this afternoon, the high will weaken to 30.2 inches along the Hudson Bay shore of northern Ontario while the Colorado Low moves to the Missouri River basin, weakening to 29.6 inches. This low weakens further to 29.7 inches as it shifts over northern Lake Michigan Tuesday morning while the high progresses into Quebec, sending troughing to 29.8 inches over Lake Superior on Tuesday. Ridging dominates over Lake Superior midweek as the low continues marching east and high pressure of 30.2 inches builds over the Dakotas by Wednesday afternoon. The high further builds to 30.3 inches over Lake Superior Wednesday night while a 29.7 inch low develops over Saskatchewan. By Thursday evening, this low weakens to 29.9 inches over northern Ontario as the high moves to New England. Behind the low, expansive 30.7 inch high builds over eastern Montana before expanding over the Plains for Friday. Pressure increases rapidly over the Upper Great Lakes Friday afternoon into Saturday, reaching 30.4 inches by Saturday morning, then decreasing

marineWeather.synopsis: Broad low pressure around 29.5 inches over the central Plains to Minnesota will drive south-southwesterly winds through today. This low is expected to lift into central Wisconsin by this evening. Expecting scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to develop tonight as the low approaches and crosses the open waters. Winds shift to northwesterly on Tuesday as an associated cold front crosses the lake and the low pressure exits east. The front may stall just south of the lake Tuesday night, with a light northerly breeze across the lake and shower/thunderstorm potential towards the southern end of the lake. High pressure around 30.2 inches building into the northern Plains will keep winds northerly into Wednesday, turning northeasterly Wednesday night and easterly into Thursday as the high pressure passes north of the lake and low pressure of 29.9 inches develops near Missouri/Illinois. Low pressure looks to cross Lake Michigan Thursday night, with strong high pressure building from western Canada into the Dakotas/Nebraska into Friday. Expect strong northwest winds Friday through Friday night, with high confidence in widespread gales. A few gusts approaching storm force could be po

Low pressure, 29.60 inches, will then push from the central Plains into the Great Lakes tomorrow morning, bringing the next potential for rain showers and isolated thunderstorms. Departure of this system will then facilitate the passage of a cold front Wednesday morning, bringing breezy northwest flow across northern Lake Huron.

High pressure 30.00 inches builds to the south of Lake Erie today and persists through Tuesday. Low pressure 29.70 inches moves through the Great Lakes late Tuesday with a cold front sweeping across the lake early Wednesday. High pressure 30.20 briefly builds across the Great Lakes on Thursday followed by low pressure 29.60 inches moving through on Friday.

A ridge averaging 29.9 inches will slide eastward across the lower Great Lakes today before exiting eastward tonight. A cold front will sweep southeast across the lake on Tuesday. Behind the cold front, a ridge averaging 30.2 inches builds from northern Ontario through Thursday. A 29.9 inch low may move across the Great Lakes region Friday. This low has the potential to deepen into a stronger low.
